title: Explain the coin flip posterior
summary: A one-line documentation addition to the coin flip example README that names the closed-form posterior, Beta(24, 18).

blocks.text:
MCMC.js is a command-line tool that runs Bayesian models, checks sampler convergence and reports results. The coin flip example is the introductory model: it estimates the heads probability p of a coin with a uniform Beta(1, 1) prior and the README states the data as 23 heads in 40 tosses.

This PR adds one sentence after the existing line that says p concentrates near 0.575. The new sentence states that the posterior is Beta(24, 18) with the Beta(1, 1) prior. Only examples/coin_flip/README.md changes. No code, model files or data files change, so there is no API or compatibility impact.

blocks.title: README text after the run command
blocks.before: The data has 23 heads in 40 tosses, so `p` concentrates near 0.575.
blocks.after:
The data has 23 heads in 40 tosses, so `p` concentrates near 0.575.
The posterior is `Beta(24, 18)` with the `Beta(1, 1)` prior.

blocks.text: Source review of the README text only. The conjugate update is correct for the stated inputs: a Beta(1, 1) prior plus 23 heads and 17 tails gives Beta(1+23, 1+17) = Beta(24, 18). The claim depends on the README's own statement of the data. I did not read coin_flip.jl, coin_flip.stan or data.csv to confirm that they match 23 heads in 40 tosses.

blocks.title: 0.575 is the posterior mode, not the mean
blocks.text: For Beta(24, 18) the mode is (24-1)/(24+18-2) = 23/40 = 0.575 and the mean is 24/42 ≈ 0.571. The adjacent text says p concentrates near 0.575, which is accurate as a statement about the mode. Now that the posterior is named, a reader may compare the 0.575 figure with the mean in the mcmc run summary and see a small difference. If the PR's aim is to help readers relate the closed-form posterior to the sampler output, naming the quantity would avoid that. This is optional wording and not a defect.

blocks.title: Optional wording: name the mode and the mean
blocks.text: Keeps the PR's purpose of explaining the posterior. It only states which summary 0.575 is and adds the mean the sampler should be near.
blocks.before:
The data has 23 heads in 40 tosses, so `p` concentrates near 0.575.
The posterior is `Beta(24, 18)` with the `Beta(1, 1)` prior.
blocks.after:
The data has 23 heads in 40 tosses. With the `Beta(1, 1)` prior the posterior is
`Beta(24, 18)`, with mode 0.575 and mean about 0.571.
